title: Tensor base change of relatively flat finitely presented modules with proper support on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S,T,T'$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T,T'$ over $S$, and let $g:T'\to T$ be an $S$-morphism. Let $f:X\to T$ be a locally finite type morphism from an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $X'=X\times_T T'$ with projection $p:X'\to X$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], of finite presentation: etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Say $M$ is flat over $T$ when for each etale scheme chart $U\to X$ and each $u\in U$ the stalk $M_u=\operatorname{colim}_{u\in W}M(W)$, over the Zariski open neighbourhoods $W\subseteq U$ of $u$, is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for the image $t$ of $u$ in $T$, through $\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{U,u}$; this is the stalkwise flatness of [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] on each chart. Say $M$ has support proper over $T$ when there exist a representable closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to T$ proper [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $G$ such that $i_*G\simeq M$; finite type means etale locally finitely generated. If $M$ is flat over $T$ and has support proper over $T$, then the tensor pullback $p^*M$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] is quasi-coherent, of finite presentation, flat over $T'$, and has support proper over $T'$ in these same senses. No flatness, noetherianity or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $g$, and no finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is needed.

proof.text: Write $H=p^*M$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent] to $p$ to obtain that $H$ is quasi-coherent. The separate assertion "Tensor pullback preserves finite presentation" in [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-limit-category] applies to the arbitrary morphism $p$ and gives finite presentation of $H$; its inverse-limit clauses are not used. Thus these assertions require neither a flat base change nor a finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$.

Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $u:U\to X$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Set $U'=U\times_TT'$ and write $b:U'\to U$ and $u':U'\to X'$. The fibre-product property and preservation of etale coverings in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] make $U'$ a scheme and $u'$ a surjective etale chart. Restrict $M$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ and let $N$ be its restriction to Zariski opens. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $N$ is quasi-coherent; the definition of relative flatness in the statement says exactly that $N$ is flat over $T$. Apply [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback] to the cartesian scheme square $U'=U\times_TT'$ to see that $b^*N$ is flat over $T'$. The tensor-pullback comparison in [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], applied to $p:X'\to X$ and $u:U\to X$, gives $H|_{U'}\simeq b_{\mathrm{et}}^*(M|_U)$. The pullback comparison in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies its Zariski restriction with $b^*N$. Hence the actual restriction of $H$ to the chart $U'$ is flat over $T'$.

source.place: Tag 05VW, lemma-base-change-module-flat (1), proof by etale scheme charts; with scheme relative flatness base change

proof.text: This also gives the required flatness on every chart, not merely the chosen one. Let $w:W\to X'$ be any etale scheme chart and set $E=W\times_{X'}U'$. Both projections $a:E\to W$ and $c:E\to U'$ are etale scheme maps, and $a$ is surjective, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the scheme-test meaning of etale in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The Zariski modules $Q=H|_W$ and $L=H|_{U'}$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Etale restriction is tensor pullback by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]; the same scheme comparison identifies $a^*Q\simeq c^*L$ with the restriction of $H$ to $E$. Etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The pointwise assertion of [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] for $c$ and step 2 imply that $c^*L$ is flat over $T'$. The surjective-flat-family assertion of that node, applied to the singleton cover $a$, then implies that $Q$ is flat over $T'$. In particular every stalk on $W$ has the stipulated flatness over the corresponding local ring of $T'$. Since $W$ was arbitrary, $H$ is flat over $T'$ in exactly the stated stalkwise sense.

source.place: Tag 02JZ, lemma-flat-permanence, with the etale-chart reduction of spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05VW

proof.text: Choose the carrier in the hypothesis, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, with $Z\to T$ proper, and a finite type quasi-coherent $G$ with $i_*G\simeq M$. Put $Z'=Z\times_TT'$. The universal property of fibre products identifies $Z'$ with $Z\times_XX'$: a map to either space is a pair of maps to $Z$ and $T'$ with equal composites to $T$. Write $q:Z'\to Z$ and $i':Z'\to X'$. This uses [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $i'$ is a representable closed immersion: for any scheme test $V\to X'$ its pullback is $Z\times_X V\to V$, a closed immersion by the scheme-test definition of $i$. Equivalently, one can apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] after scheme testing. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] applied to $Z\to T$ and $g$, the morphism $Z'\to T'$ is proper. Neither conclusion uses reducedness of $Z'$ or flatness of $g$.

source.place: Tag 02YW, lemma-base-change-immersions; spaces-morphisms.tex proper base change; carrier formulation of spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CZI

proof.text: Set $G'=q^*G$, which is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. To check finite type, use the local generator presentations of $G$. Tensor pullback is left adjoint to module direct image by [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], so [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] says it preserves cokernels and finite sums. For any such pullback $a$, the tensor formula gives $a^*\mathcal O\simeq\mathcal O$ by $r\otimes s\mapsto r\,a^\sharp(s)$, inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$; their two composites are identities by the tensor balancing relation. Thus it sends a finite free module of rank $n$ to one of rank $n$ and a surjection from it to a surjection. On an etale cover of $Z$ presenting generators of $G$, pull the cover back to $Z'$, and refine by scheme charts. These are coverings by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Localization and tensor pullback commute by the tensor-pullback comparison of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]; the enlargement in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] permits the intermediate covering objects to be algebraic spaces. On each resulting chart the pulled generator presentation is therefore $\mathcal O^n\twoheadrightarrow G'$. This is exactly the stipulated finite-type condition. The argument uses only finite sums and cokernels, not preservation of kernels.

proof.text:
The closed immersion $i$ is affine in the scheme-test sense: for every affine scheme $V\to X$, its pullback is a closed immersion into $V$, whose source is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] to $f=i$, $g=p$, $F=G$ and the cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_XX'$. Its hypotheses hold because $G$ is quasi-coherent and $i$ is affine; it requires no flatness of $p$. Its canonical isomorphism gives
$$p^*i_*G\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*q^*G=i'_*G'.$$
Apply the functor $p^*$ to the isomorphism $i_*G\simeq M$ and compose to obtain $i'_*G'\simeq H$.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change; affine closed immersions: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 07U2, lemma-closed-immersion-affine

proof.text: The pair $(i':Z'\hookrightarrow X',G')$ from steps 4--6 is a carrier with $Z'\to T'$ proper, $G'$ finite type and quasi-coherent, and $i'_*G'\simeq p^*M$. It therefore witnesses proper support in precisely the existential sense stated in the hypothesis. Combine this with finite presentation and quasi-coherence from step 1 and relative flatness from steps 2--3. The empty chart and zero module cause no exception: all local assertions are vacuous on empty schemes and tensor pullback preserves zero. No part of the argument added a hypothesis on $g$ or a finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$.

lean.statement: theorem moduleTensorPullback_flat_properSupport_baseChange {S : Scheme.{u}} (T T' : Over S) (g : T' ⟶ T) (X X' : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ schemeSpace T') (sq : IsPullback p.hom f'.hom f.hom (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map g⟩ : schemeSpace T' ⟶ schemeSpace T).hom) (hf : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) f) (M : X.Modules) (hqc : M.IsQuasicoherent) (hfp : M.IsFinitePresentation) (hflat : ∀ U : X.EtaleSite, ((schemeRestriction X U).obj M).IsFlatOver (yoneda.preimage (U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom)).left) (hsupp : ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ a ↦ IsClosedImmersion a.left) i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∃ G : Z.Modules, G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsFiniteType ∧ Nonempty ((moduleDirectImage i).obj G ≅ M)) : ((moduleTensorPullback p).obj M).IsQuasicoherent ∧ ((moduleTensorPullback p).obj M).IsFinitePresentation ∧ (∀ U : X'.EtaleSite, ((schemeRestriction X' U).obj ((moduleTensorPullback p).obj M)).IsFlatOver (yoneda.preimage (U.obj.hom ≫ f'.hom.hom)).left) ∧ (∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ X'), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ a ↦ IsClosedImmersion a.left) i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (i ≫ f') ∧ ∃ G : Z.Modules, G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsFiniteType ∧ Nonempty ((moduleDirectImage i).obj G ≅ (moduleTensorPullback p).obj M))
